Article Title: 'Inspired by Rahul Gandhi': BJP targets AISA's Neha Bora over 'Brahmanvaad' remarks
Article Text:
​BJP calls AISA chief Neha Bora 'poster girl' of Rahul Gandhi's 'anti-Hindu politics'

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Tuesday targeted All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora over a video purportedly showing her criticising the "Brahmanical system" with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accusing her of spreading "Hindu hate".Sharing the video on X, Bhandari described Bora as the "poster girl" of what he called Rahul Gandhi 's anti-Hindu politics.In the video, Bora is heard speaking about the safety of women and criticising the Brahmanical system. She reportedly cited the Unnao and Kathua cases during her remarks.Bhandari also linked Bora's comments to an earlier remark by the Congress leader about the harassment of women."Neha Bora poster girl of Rahul Gandhi displays her Hindu hate," Bhandari wrote.He added, "She is inspired from Rahul Gandhi who earlier had said 'Mandiro main ladkiyon ke sath ched chad hoti hai'.""Congress Hates Hindus, loves vote bank! Congress Soch is a threat to India's unity!" Bhandari posted.The BJP spokesperson's remarks came after the video surfaced on social media, triggering a political row over Bora's statements. The video is undated, and the circumstances in which the remarks were made could not be independently verified.Bora has been actively involved in the ongoing protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.She participated in the October 10 protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organisations against the CEC in Delhi. The demonstration saw police detain several protesters, including Bora, as authorities imposed restrictions on gatherings in parts of the national capital.The AISA leader also backed the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally against the CEC, urging people to join the opposition's demonstration in Delhi. She has also been seen alongside Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders during the protests.The protests have centred on allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and demands for Kumar's resignation. Meanwhile, the Election Commission has denied allegations of wrongdoing in the electoral roll revision process.
Article Summary: BJP calls AISA chief Neha Bora 'poster girl' of Rahul Gandhi's 'anti-Hindu politics' Party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accuses Bora of spreading "Hindu hate" Video purportedly shows Bora criticising the "Brahmanical system"

Article Title: Unhappy with Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, six NCP biggies meet Amit Shah
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah met senior NCP leaders at his residence amid growing concerns over internal differences in the party following Ajit Pawar's death

NCP leaders Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal and others attended a meeting with Amit Shah in Delhi, amid reports of discontent over Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth's leadership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI/PUNE: With BJP concerned over organisational discord within NCP, home minister Amit Shah late Sunday met senior functionaries believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and nudged them to resolve their internal rift in the interest of the party.The meeting was attended by NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and netas Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Neither deputy CM Sunetra nor Parth was present. Sunetra then called a core committee meet in Mumbai.Sources said the dissidents' concerns remained unresolved after talks with Sunetra, Parth and his younger sibling Jay. Days ahead will prove crucial for NCP, which is a part of the BJP-led NDA.The rift has been brewing over what confidants of late Ajit Pawar see as Parth's attempt to push important decisions through his mother without consulting them. Ajit's sudden death in a plane crash had thrust Sunetra into the leadership. The immediate trigger appeared to be NCP's loss in the lone MLC seat it contested. The Sharad Pawar-led faction won two seats, suggesting some family loyalists may have returned to veteran's camp.At the meeting with Shah, the group aired grievances, particularly about Parth allegedly riding roughshod over the party, with his mother allowing him to have his way.NCP seniors, who sided with Ajit during the split with Sharad Pawar, did not criticise Sunetra. However, they resented her allowing Parth to repeatedly call the shots, suggesting she backed him, an unhappy party member said. "Having grown in a political family and married into Pawar clan, she has enough smarts not to sense the unease among seniors," he said.Ajit's confidants at Shah's residence underlined Sunetra and Parth's isolation.BJP believes organisational discord in NCP could help opposition, especially NCP-SP, regain ground in western Maharashtra and hurt the governing coalition. Shinde-led Shiv Sena is its third partner. Shinde, a Maratha like Pawars, could use NCP's decline to gain leverage over BJP.Merger talks between two NCP factions were also raised at Shah's residence, sources said. Tatkare rejected suggestions that discussions continued. "The curtains have drawn on merger issue. Even seniors of the other NCP faction have said so," he said after the core committee meeting. Hours earlier, NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule had attended INDIA bloc rally in Delhi.Tatkare claimed there were no differences in the party. But functionaries held another meeting at Bhujbal's Mumbai residence, again without Sunetra or Parth. Chief spokesperson Umesh Patil said attempts were being made to give "unnecessary political colour" to Shah's meeting and create a false narrative of internal differences.
Article Summary: NCP leaders Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Chhagan Bhujbal and others attended a meeting with Amit Shah in Delhi, amid reports of discontent over Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth's leadership. Days ahead will prove crucial for NCP, which is a part of the BJP-led NDA.

Article Title: Day after quitting as Punjab MLAs, 3 AAP rebels come into BJP fold
Article Text:
Three former AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP a day after resigning, citing concerns over rising crime, drugs and gangsterism in the poll-bound state

NEW DELHI: A day after resigning as MLAs in Punjab, three AAP members joined BJP here on Monday, giving a boost to the saffron outfit in the poll-bound state.BJP is making an all-out push to emerge as a serious contender for office in the state after languishing on the margins so far.Chetan Singh Jouramajra, a former cabinet minister elected from Samana, former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who won from Amritsar North, and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, who represented Sanaur in the assembly, decried "rising" gangsterism and drug abuse in the state and expressed confidence in BJP's ability to turn things around as they joined the party.In his remarks, Vijay Pratap Singh said, "Crime, drugs, corruption and gangsterism are rampant in Punjab. Bhagwant Mann and Arvind Kejriwal have completely uprooted and destroyed AAP, which was born from a revolutionary mindset."
Article Summary: Three former AAP MLAs from Punjab join BJP a day after resigning. They cited concerns over rising crime, drugs and gangsterism in the state. BJP is making an all-out push to emerge as a serious contender for office in Punjab.

Article Title: 'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
Article Text:
The NCP's defence came even as the absence of Sunetra Pawar during the meeting with Amit Shah.

NCP leaders meet after Delhi parleys

NEW DELHI: The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) on Monday sought to put speculation about an internal rift to rest, with party leaders dismissing reports of differences following a high-profile meeting between Union Home Minister Amit Shah and a delegation of senior NCP leaders in New Delhi.The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports suggesting that Sunetra Pawar and Rajya Sabha MP Parth Pawar had been excluded from the Delhi discussions, describing the claims as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".Patil accused sections of the media of giving the meeting an unnecessary political angle and creating an impression that the party was divided."Attempts are being made to give an unnecessary political twist to the meeting and create a narrative of internal differences and lack of coordination within the party. The NCP is an important constituent of the Mahayuti alliance and remains united under the leadership of Sunetra Pawar," he said.He also urged the media to verify information before reporting on the party."Do not politicise formal meetings between leaders of alliance partners. Speculation should not be portrayed as fact," the NCP leader added.The delegation that met Shah late on Sunday included Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Dilip Walse Patil, Hassan Mushrif, Chhagan Bhujbal and Dhananjay Munde.After returning to Maharashtra, the leaders held closed-door discussions at Bhujbal's residence. Walse Patil, who was part of the delegation, told PTI that all the leaders who had met Shah had returned to the state."The core group will meet now and DCM Sunetra Pawar in the evening," Walse Patil said.Patil said Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar had met Shah earlier to discuss issues facing the party after Ajit Pawar's death. During that meeting, she had informed Shah that a delegation of senior party leaders would meet him and requested an appointment."Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar had earlier met Shah and discussed various issues facing the party following the death of Ajit Pawar. During that meeting, she had informed Shah that a delegation of senior party leaders would meet him and requested him to give them time," Patil said.He added that the delegation comprised senior leaders familiar with key decisions taken during Ajit Pawar's tenure, issues concerning Maharashtra and matters related to the party.The meeting with Shah comes after a setback for the NCP, which recently lost the Aurangabad Graduates constituency in the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections, a seat it had held for 18 years.It has also been seeking the finance portfolio, which was held by Ajit Pawar until his death in a plane crash in January this year.Against this backdrop, the absence of Sunetra Pawar and her sons from the Delhi meeting added to questions about coordination and decision-making within the party.
Article Summary: NCP rejects reports of internal rift after meeting with Amit Shah. Speculation fuelled by absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil described the claims as "incorrect, baseless and misleading" He accused sections of the media of giving the meeting an unnecessary political angle.

Article Title: Azam Khan, facing 95 cases since 2017, moves SC against his arrest by ED
Article Text:
Though the bench initially asked Khan why he did not move the Allahabad HC, it agreed to list the matter for hearing.

NEW DELHI: SP leader and ten time MLA Azam Khan on Monday moved Supreme Court challenging the ED decision to arrest him on stepping out of Rampur jail after Allahabad HC granted him bail in the last of the 95 cases, which have been slapped on him after BJP came to power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017.Advocate Mohd Nizamuddin Pasha told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the arrest by ED in a 2019 case, in which FIR itself was registered 13 years after the allegations about land purchase transactions fo Jauhar University from farmers, was illegal.Though the bench initially asked Khan why he did not move the Allahabad HC, it agreed to list the matter for hearing. Khan said he was forced to move the SC because of “blatant illegality of his arrest including the manner and timing and the gross abuse of process and mala fide exercise of power whereby the machinery of criminal justice system is used for political ends to keep an opposition leader indefinitely in incarceration particularly on account of the approaching assembly elections in UP. ”Seeking invocation of SC’s exclusive Article 142 powers for grant of interim bail, Khan said since 2017, he has been made an accused in 95 criminal cases, including the ED case. He has been acquitted in six cases, and three cases were closed after his complicity could not be proved.“He has been convicted in six; in four of these his sentence has been suspended and/or his conviction stayed, and in the other two, the sentence of two years has been undergone.The remaining 80 cases are pending trial. The clear pattern that emerges is that whenever the Petitioner is about to be released, a fresh case is registered or revived, and he is sought to be kept behind bars,” Khan alleged.The 78-year-old petitioner, who had also been a UP cabinet minister as member of both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha, complained that he was illegally arrested in a 7-year-old ECIR from the gate of District Jail Rampur on Oct 31 without providing him with the arrest memo or written grounds and reasons for arrest.Khan said, while being lodged in Rampur Jail, ED had questioned him relating to the case and recorded his statements under PMLA and hence there was no basis for the ED to arrest him against and seek judicial custody. “Timing of my arrest is wholly mala fide and politically motivated,” the SP leader said, claiming that he suffered from serious kidney, urinary and other age-related ailments. And that he has spent more than 5 years in prison since Feb 2020.
Article Summary: Azam Khan on Monday moved Supreme Court challenging the ED decision to arrest him on stepping out of Rampur jail after Allahabad HC granted him bail. Khan said he was forced to move the SC because of ‘blatant illegality of his arrest’

Article Title: Rouse Avenue court seeks Delhi Police response on Bimol Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea
Article Text:
Former JNU professor and Congress MP Bimol Akoijam (PTI file photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue Court on Tuesday issued notice to Delhi Police on the anticipatory bail plea of Manipur MP and former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Bimol Akoijam in a sexual harassment case and extended his interim protection till November 5.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought the police response and directed the investigating agency to place on record the complaint filed by JNU students against Akoijam. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5.Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station following allegations of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him when he was working as a professor at the university.Additional Public Prosecutor Manish Rawat appeared for Delhi Police and accepted the notice. The police have already filed a reply before the Patiala House Court.During the hearing, Akoijam's counsel submitted that the complaint was made by a group of students to the dean and not by any aggrieved woman directly. The counsel also said the university's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) had examined the matter and its report had been annexed to the bail application.The defence further submitted that Akoijam had cooperated with the investigation and appeared before the investigating officer, while the alleged complainant was not joining the probe. The counsel also pointed out that the high court had stayed his termination from the university.Akoijam had initially secured transit anticipatory bail from a Manipur court on October 12, which was extended till October 20 and subsequently till October 29.He then approached the Patiala House Court, which granted him interim protection till November 2. However, the court held that it could not hear his anticipatory bail plea as he is a sitting MP, and that the matter fell within the jurisdiction of the Rouse Avenue Court.The investigating officer had also opposed the plea on the jurisdictional ground. Following the transfer of the case, Akoijam moved the Rouse Avenue Court for anticipatory bail.
Article Summary: Akoijam is seeking anticipatory bail in an FIR registered at Vasant Kunj North police station. He is accused of sexual harassment levelled by 11 JNU students against him. The matter has been listed for arguments on November 5.

Article Title: 'Rs 25cr spent on ads to claim no stubble burning, FIRs tell another story': BJP targets AAP govt in Punjab
Article Text:
Rs 20-25 crore was spent on advertisements to project that there was no stubble burning in the state, said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab of allowing and facilitating stubble burning while spending Rs 20-25 crore on advertisements claiming that no farm fires were taking place in the state. He alleged that the government was then registering FIRs against farmers for stubble burning, even as it publicly denied the practice.He also questioned the appointment of former AAP spokesperson Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board, alleging that the move was aimed at manipulating pollution data.Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Sirsa claimed that Punjab had recorded more than 1,000 incidents of stubble burning and alleged that the state government was trying to conceal the extent of the problem through publicity campaigns.“Advertisements worth Rs 20-25 crore were released to claim that stubble burning was not taking place in Punjab this year. On the other hand, I am handing over copies of all the FIRs, district-wise, to you. These are all FIRs registered in connection with stubble burning,” he said, displaying documents that he claimed contained details of the cases, further alleging that "Punjab Police and Punjab government officers are facilitating the burning of stubble.Taking aim at AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Sirsa alleged that the party had brought its political spokesperson from Delhi to head the Punjab Pollution Control Board to influence the reporting of pollution data.“For the first time in Punjab's history, a non-Punjabi, non-IAS, non-technical person has been appointed to such a position. They have appointed their political spokesperson, who is said to be a close relative of Arvind Kejriwal, as the chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board after bringing her from Delhi,” Sirsa said.He identified the appointee as Reena Gupta, alleging that she was being projected as the face of the campaign to deny the scale of stubble burning in Punjab. Sirsa claimed the appointment was intended to “conceal the truth by fudging data”.Sirsa sought to contrast Punjab's situation with Delhi's air quality, claiming that the national capital had recorded 220 clean-air days in 2026, the highest in a decade. He also said October was the cleanest in the past 10 years and that the average air quality index (AQI) had improved by 10 per cent compared with previous years.Appealing to Kejriwal and AAP leader Manish Sisodia not to undermine Delhi's efforts to improve air quality, Sirsa said, “By setting fires in Punjab, you are once again causing the situation in Delhi to deteriorate.”
Article Summary: Manjinder Singh Sirsa accuses Punjab government of allowing and facilitating stubble burning while spending Rs 20-25 crore on advertisements. He also questioned the appointment of former AAP spokesperson Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board. Sirsa claimed the appointment was intended to “conceal the truth by fudging data”

Article Title: 'Doesn’t have courage to call all-party meet?’: Congress questions Shah over delay in discussion on delimitation Bill
Article Text:
Congress leader also referred to his remarks about holding a special session to discuss allegations of vote theft.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday questioned the Centre over the delay in proroguing Parliament, alleging that the government was considering convening a special session to push delimitation-related bills. He also challenged the Centre to share its proposals with the opposition and convene an all-party meeting to discuss them.In a post on X, Ramesh said 82 days had passed since the Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die, but it had still not been prorogued. He alleged that Union home minister Amit Shah was continuing to explore the possibility of calling a special session to pass the delimitation bills."The content of these Bills is still not known although its intent is clear—to save the BJP from the debacle that is staring it in 2029," Ramesh alleged.Taking a swipe at Shah, the Congress leader also referred to his remarks about holding a special session to discuss allegations of vote theft. Ramesh questioned the apparent difference in the government's approach, recalling that Shah had earlier declined the opposition's demand for a debate on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying it was the Election Commission's prerogative."Meanwhile, the self-styled Chanakya, the master of bluff, bombast and bluster says he is ready for a Special Session to discuss vote chori.Last year, when the combined Opposition wanted a debate on SIR he had refused saying SIR was the prerogative of the Election Commission.If the Home Minister is serious about a Special Session on vote chori, he should first secure the resignation of his hatchet man CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He should also suspend SIR," Ramesh said.He further demanded that the government share its proposed delimitation changes with the Opposition well in advance and asked why Shah was not convening an all-party meeting to discuss the proposals in detail."Why doesn't he have the courage to convene an All-Party meeting to discuss these proposals in detail?" Ramesh asked.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the Centre over the delay in proroguing Parliament. He alleged that the government was considering convening a special session to push delimitation-related bills. He also challenged the Centre to share its proposals with the opposition and convene an all-party meeting to discuss them.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday hit back at Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi after he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of becoming PM and remaining in office with the help of foreign forces. BJP spokesperson C R Kesavan questioned Rahul's foreign visits and alleged that the Congress leader had sought foreign interference in India's internal affairs.In a post on X, Kesavan called Rahul a "lousy con artist" and accused him of making misleading claims that backfire. You became PM because of foreign help. You remain PM because of foreign help. Your financial system is fully controlled and supported by foreigners. Article Title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
Article Text:
BJP calls INDIA bloc’s ‘vote chori’ rally a flop, Shah takes jibe at Rahul Gandhi’s PM ambitions

CHANDIGARH/NEW DELHI: BJP derided INDIA bloc's rally against 'vote chori' as a "flop show", while Union minister Amit Shah said Rahul Gandhi could hope to be PM only in a 'mock parliament', referring to Congress's mock CEC impeachment.Addressing a gathering on Chandigarh Police's 60th Raising Day on Sunday, Shah said Sonia Gandhi had resorted to the move since her dream of Rahul becoming PM was not fulfilled. "You (Rahul) want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life; your turn won't come," Shah said.His remarks highlighted BJP’s counterpunch to the opposition’s campaign against Election Commission and govt over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with BJP functionaries, including CMs, participating in ‘Save Democracy, Defeat Anarchy’ marches across the country.BJP president Nitin Nabin, who travelled to Rohtak as part of the anti-Congress campaign, accused Rahul of deliberately destroying the credibility of constitutional bodies as part of his plan to sow anarchy.As BJP functionaries, like former party chief and Union health minister J P Nadda, expressed jubilation over what they called a “super flop show” at Ramlila Maidan, the party also homed in on Congress’s choice of the date for the rally — the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots which took place in the wake of former PM Indira Gandhi’s assassination — to accuse the opposition party of mocking the tragedy suffered by the community.“They chose the very day when genocide of Sikhs happened to hold a rally. It is like rubbing salt into the wounds of 1984 victims,” said Shah in Chandigarh. Recalling Rajiv Gandhi’s controversial “when a big tree falls, the earth shakes” remark, which was seen by many as the former PM seeking to rationalise the mass killings of Sikhs, a combative Shah emphasised that BJP had urged Congress not to hold the rally between Nov 1 and 3, days associated with the massacre.Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis, joined by deputy CM Eknath Shinde, led the march in Thane, while CM Pushkar Singh Dhami and CM Rekha Gupta led similar anti-Congress protests in Uttarakhand and Delhi, respectively.Former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan along with Union minister Kishanpal Gujjar led a march in Faridabad. Assam CM Himata Biswa Sarma joined a protest at Shimla alongside former CM Jairam Thakur and former Union minister Anurag Thakur. Poll-bound Uttar Pradesh saw six BJP rallies. Charges of “anarchy” and “undemocratic conduct” were the themes across the rallies, with party functionaries like Union minister Bhupendra Yadav alleging that Congress’s anti-SIR protest was a ploy to mask Rahul Gandhi’s repeated political failures.
Article Summary: BJP calls INDIA bloc’s ‘vote chori’ rally a flop, Shah takes jibe at Rahul Gandhi's PM ambitions. Shah said Sonia Gandhi had resorted to the move since her dream of Rahul becoming PM was not fulfilled.

Article Title: 'Rahul Gandhi has no vision, will be responsible for Congress's wipeout': BJP's Nitin Nabin at anti-SIR march
Article Text:
Nabin criticised opposition leaders who gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday.

NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Monday targeted Rahul Gandhi , saying the Congress leader had "no vision" and would be responsible for the party's "wipeout".The BJP chief made the remarks while leading the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, End Anarchy) march in Kolkata.West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and several senior party leaders joined the rally organised as part of the BJP's counter-campaign against opposition protests over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls."Rahul has no vision, he will be responsible for Congress's wipeout," Nabin said. "Rahul spoke against the misrule of Mamata regime during Bengal polls; now both sharing stage," he added.The BJP chief further accused Rahul of being part of a "toolkit of foreign forces trying to destabilise India".He also warned Rahul to learn from his mistakes, saying, "I tell Rahul Gandhi - learn from your mistakes. Otherwise, in the days to come, there would be no one left in the country to take the name of Congress.."Nabin also criticised opposition leaders who gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against the SIR exercise."Yesterday, at Delhi's Ramleela Maidan, these people were shedding tears in the despair of defeat. But the people of the country will give them a befitting reply, just as the people of West Bengal have done," he said.Nabin also targeted the INDIA bloc parties, claiming they had suffered electoral defeats in several states."People of INDIA bloc, who were defeated in their respective states, had gathered in Delhi to cry. The manner in which TMC was wiped out in Bengal, Congress and AAP were wiped out in Delhi,” he said.“In Bihar too, RJD was completely wiped out. Now, it is Uttar Pradesh's turn, we had defeated Akhilesh Yadav earlier too and we will defeat him in 2027 too. Such people with anarchist mindsets are led by Rahul Gandhi...People of Bengal have given freedom from Mamata didi as well as from Rahul Gandhi in Delhi..." he added."There is no use in crying anymore," he said, referring to former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee 's participation in the rally.The BJP's march began at College Street and proceeded towards Dharmatala in central Kolkata, with hundreds of BJP supporters taking part. Nabin, Adhikari and state BJP president Shamik Bhattacharya held national flags during the rally.The BJP has organised similar programmes in several cities, accusing opposition parties of spreading misinformation and creating unrest over the electoral roll revision exercise.Addressing party workers ahead of the march, BJP spokesperson Debjit Sarkar said the programme was aimed at countering attempts by opposition parties to create anarchy.
Article Summary: The BJP chief made the remarks while leading the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, End Anarchy) march in Kolkata. Nabin also criticised opposition leaders who gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against the electoral roll revision exercise.

Article Title: '3 crore Bangladeshi infiltrators don't exist on voters' list': Amit Shah counters Rahul's anti-SIR pitch
Article Text:
Home minister Amit Shah said the Congress intends to "capture elections through bogus voting".

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Monday unleashed a polemical assault on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the Speical Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has become a major political flashpoint.In a verbal blitzkrieg, a day after Rahul's mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in the national capital, Shah said the Congress's criticism of the roll revision was driven by an "attempt to protect illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators", claiming that three crore such voters did not even exist.On the biggest claim by the opposition that 13 crore voters have been deleted during the electoral roll purge, Amit Shah said: "6.25 crore voters have simply relocated to new addresses, around 3 crore are deceased, and approximately 1 crore represent duplicate entries. The remaining 3 crore do not even exist — they are Bangladeshi infiltrators".Lashing out at the Lok Sabha leader of opposition, the home minister said the Congress intends to "capture elections through bogus voting".Shah said: "If one person has two votes, should one of them be cancelled or not? Now we come to the source of 'Rahul Baba's' stomach ache. Three crore votes are such that the people they belong to do not even exist.These are Bangladeshi infiltrators."He also attacked Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy, saying no matter the effort he puts along with Rahul Gandhi, the BJP will "ensure that every single infiltrator is removed from the voter list and driven out of the country."The Union home minister also countered Rahul's "Modi won because of the SIR claim", saying: "I want to ask Rahul ji: In 2014, Modi ji won. There was no SIR then, was there? So, did Modi ji win because of the SIR? He won because of the votes of the people. Modi ji won in 2019 as well. There was no SIR then. Did Modi ji win or not? He won because of the voters of India. After 2024, we won in Maharashtra with the biggest majority. We won in Haryana with the biggest majority. After 30 years, we won in Delhi. We won in Bihar with the biggest majority. In Bengal too, Didi's entire political standing has been wiped out.""The entire Congress and its allies are working to stop the SIR because these infiltrators are their vote bank. But we, the workers of the Bharatiya Janata Party , stand firmly with the SIR." Only those who are citizens of this country will be allowed to vote here," Shah said.Later, Shah went on to credit Sadar Vallabhbhai Patel, saying: "If Sardar Patel had not made the Nizam bow down at that time, Hyderabad would not be a part of India today."Amit Shah led ‘Maha Padyatra’ here on Monday as part of BJP’s nationwide campaign to counter the anti-SIR campaign launched by the INDIA bloc.He began the foot march from Babu Jagjivan Ram Statue at Basheerbagh in the heart of the city along with several party leaders and hundreds of party workers.Holding the national flag, Amit Shah was walking with Union ministers G Kishan Reddy, Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao, party MPs, MLAs, MLCs and other leaders.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah unleashed a polemical assault on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the Speical Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Shah said the Congress's criticism of the roll revision was driven by an "attempt to protect illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators", claiming that three crore such voters did not even exist.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Article Title: MP spurious liquor cases: Congress functionary held in cop's death case, spokesperson also arrested in Dewas
Article Text:
Rahul Jaiswal, who has ties to the Congress party, was detained after a police officer's death.





BHOPAL: Rahul Jaiswal, detained in connection with the death of a police officer during an anti-illicit liquor operation in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district, has allegedly told police that he is associated with the Congress and holds a 30% stake in a liquor shop linked to the smuggling network.State Congress spokesperson Anand Jain Kasliwal was also arrested in connection with deaths allegedly caused by spurious liquor in Dewas, police said.A video of Jaiswal being questioned by police was shared with the media by an officer from the investigation team led by Special Director General of Police Upendra Jain. In the video, Jaiswal can allegedly be heard saying that he is currently the Congress in-charge of the Khategaon Assembly constituency and served as the district Youth Congress president from 2018 to 2024-25.The case pertains to the death of Khategaon station house officer (SHO) Dilip Puri early Monday. Puri had reached a spot along the Indore-Betul highway after receiving information about illicit liquor smuggling. When he attempted to question the driver of a truck parked near a roadside eatery, the driver allegedly drove over the road divider while trying to flee. The truck's rear wheel ran over Puri.Apart from Jaiswal, police have detained two other accused, Keram Singh Changod and Vijay Rao, in connection with the case.According to officials, Jaiswal operated an illicit liquor smuggling network from Timarni in Harda district to Gujarat. Changod allegedly arranged the truck for driver Gajendra alias Akku Rawat, while Rao reportedly admitted to working for Jaiswal in the smuggling operation.Jaiswal told police that he was originally from Timarni and that he, along with Indore resident Manish Jaiswal, Ahmedabad resident Mohit Jaiswal and Patan Jaiswal, were partners in the liquor shop he managed.Madhya Pradesh Cabinet minister Vishwas Sarang claimed that Rahul Jaiswal and his brother Manish Jaiswal were partners in the liquor shop linked to the case. He also alleged that Rahul Jaiswal was close to state Congress president Jitu Patwari and held charge of the party's Khategaon Assembly constituency.Sarang said the shop's manager, Bhupendra Rana, had provided important information to police.The incident triggered a political confrontation between the Congress and the BJP. The Congress attacked the state government over law and order, alleging that the liquor mafia was effectively running Madhya Pradesh and the government was acting as a mute spectator.The BJP hit back, citing the alleged involvement of a Congress functionary in the case. It also questioned whether money generated through the illicit liquor trade was being used to pay the Congress state office's electricity bills and fund party protests and other expenses.There was no response from Congress leaders to Jaiswal's alleged statements. Attempts to contact them for comment proved unsuccessful.
Article Summary: Rahul Jaiswal, detained in connection with the death of a police officer during an anti-illicit liquor operation in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district. He allegedly told police that he is associated with the Congress and holds a 30% stake in a liquor shop linked to the smuggling network. State Congress spokesperson Anand Jain Kasliwal was also arrested.

Article Title: Andhra Pradesh municipal election results 2026 Live Updates: NDA leads in most civic bodies, heads for sweeping win
Article Text:
Counting begins at Andhra University

NDA is set to sweep the municipal polls, with its nominees leading in almost all municipal corporations and a majority of municipalities in the state. The TDP-led NDA is expected to win more than 90% of the wards/divisions in urban civic bodies.

The counting covers 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.

Counting in Chirala was postponed to Nov 6 due to heavy rain in the coastal town

Election observer Tej Bharat, along with District Election Officer S. Ramsundar Reddy, inspected the vote counting process at the municipal vote counting centre. They reached the strong rooms at Rajiv Sports Ground and gave instructions to officials to ensure that the counting of votes is done in a transparent manner.

Tirupati recorded the lowest polling percentage at 47% in the municipal elections. Counting of votes in 66 municipal divisions has begun.

In Visakhapatnam, officials and agents arrived at a counting centre near Andhra University Engineering College, where preparations and security arrangements were in place

The elections were held on November 1, with polling conducted from 7 am to 5 pm. Repolling, wherever required, was conducted on November 2

The 13 municipal corporations include Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Guntur, Nellore, Kurnool, Kadapa and Tirupati.

The Vijayawada Municipal Corporation mayoral contest is among the closely watched electoral battles, with NDA-backed Jana Sena candidate Vangaveeti Radhakrishna, YSR Congress Party candidate and former mayor Rayana Bhagyalakshmi, and independent candidate A B Venkateswara Rao, a former Director General of Police, in the fray.

The civic poll results are being viewed as a significant political test for the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), led by Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, following its victory in the 2024 Assembly elections.

The results are also expected to indicate the electoral standing of the opposition YSR Congress Party in the state's urban centres.

Earlier on Sunday, the YSRCP alleged a discrepancy in Pulivendula's polling figures, questioning how 681 votes were recorded under the ‘Others’ category when the official voter list reportedly had only 14 voters in that category.

YSRCP president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy met the Returning Officer (RO) in Pulivendula and submitted a representation alleging irregularities during polling.

Reddy alleged that around 70 YSRCP polling agents were not allowed to enter polling booths and demanded the Returning Officer's intervention to ensure a fair polling process.

Following the meeting, he staged a sit-in protest outside the Returning Officer's office in Pulivendula, demanding justice for the party's polling agents.





VISAKHAPATNAM: Counting of votes in 92 urban local bodies across Andhra Pradesh began on Tuesday, with election officials and polling agents arriving at designated counting centres amid security arrangements across the state.
Article Summary: NDA is set to sweep the municipal polls, with its nominees leading in almost all municipal corporations and a majority of municipalities. The TDP-led NDA is expected to win more than 90% of the wards/divisions in urban civic bodies. Counting of votes in 66 municipal divisions has begun.

Article Title: Man poses as CM Devendra Fadnavis’s aide, extorts Rs 3.2cr from contractor
Article Text:
The police arrested Asif Ismail Pathan (40), a native of Aurangabad.(AI Image)





MUMBAI: The Marine Drive police have arrested an Aurangabad resident who impersonated an Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , and under the pretext of clearing a private contractor’s pending PWD bills worth Rs 50 crore, extorted Rs 3.5 crore from a civil contractor.Even after paying Rs 3.25 crore in cash, the accused kept on demanding another Rs 75 lakh, threatening that the Rs 3.25 crore already paid would be lost and the pending bills would not be cleared if he failed to pay.The police arrested Asif Ismail Pathan (40), a native of Aurangabad. He was produced before the court and remanded to police custody. While seeking his custody, police said they are yet to arrest his accomplices, recover the cash, and recover the vehicle used in the crime. Police said that they suspect that the accused and his accomplices have cheated a few other people with a similar modus operandi. The court remanded him to police custody till Nov 6.Akola-based complainant Ranjitsingh Oberoi of Oberoi Construction had last month filed an FIR alleging that the accused, posing as a senior ministry official at Mantralaya and under the pretext of clearing his company’s pending PWD bills worth Rs 50 crore, extorted Rs 3.5 crore.Based on his complaint, the Marine Drive police registered an FIR against an unknown person under the BNS sections of impersonation, extortion, criminal intimidation and criminal conspiracy.Oberoi alleged that he was subsequently put in touch with another person claiming to have the final authority to approve PWD bills. Fearing financial losses and the possible collapse of his business, he arranged Rs 1.25 crore from his hotel business, construction company, and friends and travelled to Mumbai on Sept 10 and handed over the money through an alleged associate described as the caller’s bodyguard outside Hotel Trident at Nariman Point. The complainant alleged that the accused later demanded the remaining commission and collected another Rs 2 crore on Sept 15 through the same associate, who arrived in a Toyota Innova car bearing registration number MH20 HB 5666.Oberoi further alleged that on Sept 29, the caller demanded another Rs 75 lakh, threatening that the Rs 3.25 crore already paid would be lost and the pending bills would not be cleared if he failed to pay.The contractor subsequently learnt that another contractor had allegedly received a similar call in connection with pending bills. He said he visited Mantralaya on Sept 30 and discovered that the mobile number used by the caller did not belong to Mahale and that the person he had met was not govt official.
Article Summary: The police arrested Asif Ismail Pathan (40), a native of Aurangabad. He was produced before the court and remanded to police custody. Police said they are yet to arrest his accomplices, recover the cash, and recover the vehicle.

Article Title: Bengaluru top cop links Siddaramaiah sting phone to HD Kumaraswamy's Delhi residence
Article Text:
Former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah, Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh, and H.D. Kumaraswamy





BENGALURU: The mobile phone allegedly used to upload a “fabricated” video as a sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah with allegations of sexual abuse exchanged hands at the official Delhi residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy, according to Bengaluru City police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh.“Accused Ritesh Pandey, arrested in the case, had confessed the phone was exchanged at Kumaraswamy’s residence. However, investigators are yet to establish who else was involved in the exchange and the extent of their roles in the alleged conspiracy.”A senior officer, though, clarified they had only stated that the minister’s residence was used for the exchange of the phone.According to preliminary investigation, Pandey allegedly worked in coordination with Vinod Sharma, a freelance social media content creator, and Prajwal Prasad, an alleged member of the JD(S) social media wing, to procure the mobile phone.Notices have been issued to both Sharma, a Delhi resident, and Prajwal, who is from Bengaluru. However, both are absconding.According to the police commissioner, Sharma and Ritesh were instructed by Prajwal to purchase a device using Aadhaar credentials in Delhi’s Karol Bagh. The phone was then handed over to Prajwal. Ritesh was arrested in Delhi on Oct 24.
Article Summary: The mobile phone allegedly used to upload a “fabricated” video as a sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah. The phone exchanged hands at the official Delhi residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy, according to Bengaluru City police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh.
