Article Title: Gang robs 3 of gold jewellery on Mahalaxmi Express near Satara
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





A gang of thieves allegedly robbed three women passengers of gold jewellery worth around Rs 2 lakh after stopping Mumbai-Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Express by tampering with the railway signal system near Salpa station in Satara district around 2.30am on Sunday.Taking advantage of the halt, five to six gang members allegedly entered reserved coach S2 and targeted sleeping women passengers. They snatched their gold jewellery and fled.Separate cases have been registered with Lonand RPF for signal vandalism and Miraj railway police for the jewellery theft. Police are investigating the incident with the help of a dog squad and a forensic team.Sunita Gorakshnath Tupe (40), a Kanjurmarg East resident, lodged a complaint at Miraj Govt Railway Police (GRP) station. The stolen jewellery also belonged to fellow passenger Surekha Babasaheb Khade (40), a resident of Khopoli in Raigad district. The women were travelling to Kolhapur to attend a family function.Inspector Sitaram Phand of Miraj railway police, said, “The gang comprised around eight to ten members, with five to six of them allegedly entering the coaches. Some members are suspected to have remained near the signal system while others targeted passengers inside the train.”After the thieves jumped off the train, some passengers tried to chase them. However, the gang allegedly pelted stones at coaches S2, S3 and S5 while escaping, triggering panic.“The manner in which the train was stopped, followed by the robbery and stone-pelting, has raised suspicions that the incident was pre-planned. The exact manner in which the signal system was tampered with will be a key part of the investigation. We have formed several teams and a search operation is under way to trace them,” added Phand.
Article Summary: Gang of thieves allegedly robbed three women passengers of gold jewellery worth around Rs 2 lakh. They stopped Mumbai-Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Express by tampering with the railway signal system near Salpa station in Satara district around 2.30am on Sunday. Police are investigating the incident with the help of a dog squad and a forensic team.

Article Title: Polling held for contested DCC bank seats in Satara, Sangli
Article Text:
Sangli MP Vishal Patil casts vote for Sangli DCC bank

Kolhapur:





Voting for seats in the Satara and Sangli district central cooperative (DCC) banks that could not be won unopposed took place on Sunday .In Satara DCC bank, polling was held for 12 seats, with around 2,010 voters casting their votes across 11 polling booths. In Sangli, 94% of the 2,446 voters exercised their franchise for six seats. While 15 of the 21 seats in Sangli DCC bank have already been won unopposed, the Mahayuti managed to build a consensus on nine seats in Satara.Counting of votes for both banks will take place on Nov 3. The DCC banks are considered the financial lifeline of the rural economy, making their directorships politically significant. Several political stalwarts contest these elections to retain their influence over the institutions. However, under RBI rules, directors who have completed more than 10 years in office had to withdraw from the race. To ensure that control remains within their grasp, many have fielded close relatives, either getting them elected unopposed or putting them in the electoral fray.Interesting contests are unfolding in both banks. In Satara, BJP leader and state rural development minister Jaykumar Gore is facing a challenge from his brother Shekhar Gore in the Man taluka segment.A third candidate is also in the fray. In the Phaltan segment, the Naik Nimbalkar clan is once again witnessing a contest, with Sanjeevraje pitted against Samshersingh Naik Nimbalkar. In Patan, Satara guardian minister Shambhuraj Desai is facing his traditional rival Satyajit Patankar. Ministers such as Makarand Patil have been elected unopposed.In Sangli, the main contest in the Tasgaon segment is between former MLA Suman Patil, widow of late R R Patil, and former MP Sanjaykaka Patil. In the Jat segment, BJP MLA Gopichand Padalkar, who secured permission from the Supreme Court to contest the election, is facing a challenge from Vinod Pawar.
Article Summary: Voting for seats in the Satara and Sangli district central cooperative (DCC) banks that could not be won unopposed took place on Sunday. In Satara DCC bank, polling was held for 12 seats, with around 2,010 voters casting their votes. In Sangli, 94% of the 2,446 voters exercised their franchise for six seats.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai police arrest ‘RTI activist’ for threatening builder, demanding Rs 1.35 lakh
Article Text:
Tribhuvan Singh, a BJP activist and alleged RTI activist, was arrested for extortion in Navi Mumbai





NAVI MUMBAI: A 47-year-old BJP activist, who claims to be an RTI activist, and is a resident of Digha, was arrested by Rabale police on Tuesday for allegedly extorting Rs 1.35 lakh from a developer through cash and online transactions since May 2026.Police said he allegedly threatened to lodge complaints with NMMC, CIDCO and MIDC authorities claiming illegal construction on the developer’s Airoli and Digha plots and seeking their demolition.He allegedly later demanded another Rs 5,000, threatening to frame the builder’s son in a false criminal case.The arrested accused has been identified as Tribhuvan Singh. An FIR was registered on Tuesday on a complaint by developer Jitendra Pratap Singh (52), a resident of Ishwar Nagar, Digha.Based on the complainant's allegations, Rabale police invoked BNS provisions relating to extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt, criminal intimidation and intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace.Balkrushna Sawant, senior inspector of Rabale, said, "The accused Tribhuvan Singh was arrested from Mumbra area on Tuesday late evening. On Wed, he was produced before the Belapur JMFC court that remanded him to police custody for six days.This is the second time that, we have arrested the accused Singh. Previously, he was arrested in March 2025 for demanding Rs 10 lakh extortion from a builder Rushabh Gupta (29) from Gothivli, Ghansoli node and accepted Rs one lakh installment on his friend's account and kept demanding remaining amount. In that case, the accused Singh had complained to Cidco in Dec 2024 claiming illegal construction in Gothivali by the complainant builder Gupta and posted his construction site images on social media.Then, threatened hunger strike if Cidco did not demolish his illegal construction. Thereafter, he demanded the extortion amount of Rs 10 lakh for withdrawing the complaint."SI Sawant further informed, "In 2025, Singh was served with a notice of externment from Navi Mumbai for one year. But, he sought reduction in externment period for six months and got approval from zonal DCP. After returning from externment period, he again allegedly indulged in criminal activities. From 2023 till 2026, there are eight criminal cases registered against the accused Singh, including three cases at Rabale MIDC police station and one each at Rabale, Kalwa and Naupada police stations. "Meanwhile, in 2018, Singh was arrested by the Thane Anti-Extortion Cell after police laid a trap following an FIR of extortion registered against him at Kalwa police station.He was accused of trying to extort Rs 20 lakh from a local doctor by threatening to get his hospital shut down.Singh had filed multiple complaints with civic agencies against the doctor, claiming that his hospital staff was not qualified.
Article Summary: Tribhuvan Singh, 47, claims to be an RTI activist, and is a resident of Digha. He was arrested by Rabale police on Tuesday for allegedly extorting Rs 1.35 lakh from a developer. He allegedly threatened to lodge complaints with NMMC, CIDCO and MIDC authorities.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Passenger booked for trying to open emergency exit door on Delhi-Pune flight
Article Text:
Complaint was lodged against a passenger for trying to open the emergency exit door during a flight (Representative image)

Poll Vote & Share your view How should airlines handle passengers who endanger flight safety? Immediate arrest Report to authorities Banning from future flights 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PUNE: The Airport police have registered a case against a passenger for allegedly trying to open the emergency exit door of an private commercial aircraft while travelling from Delhi to Pune, thereby endangering the safety of other passengers on around 12.30 am on Monday.Omkar Vinod Kulkarni (28), an employee of a private airline, lodged a complaint at the Airport police station on Monday.Based on his complaint, a case was registered against the passenger under section 125 (penalizes any act done so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and 25 of the Aircraft Act.According to the police, the 33-year-old passenger has been served a notice. According to the police, the passenger, who resides in the Saswad area of Pune district, had gone to Delhi for some work. He was returning Pune and was travelling on the flight around 12.30am on Monday.The complainant stated that the passenger allegedly tried to open the emergency exit door without obtaining permission from the flight crew after landing.The complaint stated that only authorised crew members are permitted to operate the emergency exit door and that the passenger's act could have endangered the safety of other passengers on board.
Article Summary: Complaint was lodged against a passenger for trying to open the emergency exit door during a flight. The 33-year-old passenger has been served a notice. According to the police, the passenger, who resides in the Saswad area of Pune district, had gone to Delhi for some work. He was travelling on the flight around 12.30am on Monday.

Article Title: Duo held for stealing copper plates from KTPS
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Two men were caught red-handed while allegedly stealing copper plates worth ₹11,200 from the Koradi Thermal Power Station on Sunday. Security personnel on patrol spotted the duo removing the plates from electrical panel boards and detained them before handing them over to police.The accused have been identified as Narendra Vishwakarma (27) and Pramod Suryavanshi (28), both residents of Sillewada in Khaparkheda.According to the complaint filed by Nilesh Dudhabarve (50), a junior security officer at the Koradi Thermal Power Station, the incident took place around 2.30 pm on November 1.Two security guards deployed in the 210MW section were conducting their routine patrol when they noticed the suspects allegedly removing copper plates attached to two ISM panel boards. The plates, collectively valued at ₹11,200, were being stolen from the installation.The guards immediately intervened, caught the two men and detained them. They subsequently alerted the police, following which a team from Koradi police station reached the spot and took the suspects into custody.During questioning, the accused were identified as Vishwakarma and Suryavanshi. Police also seized the stolen copper plates and other evidence from their possession.Based on Dudhabarve's complaint, Koradi police registered a case against the duo under Section 303(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for theft and arrested them.Further investigation is underway to ascertain whether the accused were involved in similar thefts at the power plant.
Article Summary: Narendra Vishwakarma (27) and Pramod Suryavanshi (28) were caught red-handed. The plates, collectively valued at ₹11,200, were being stolen from the installation. Police also seized the stolen copper plates and other evidence from their possession.

Article Title: Ahmednagar district central cooperative bank election results today, regional leaders vie for control
Article Text:
Former MP Sujay Vikhe casts his vote during the election on Monday

Nashik:

FIR for shooting video of voting process





Voting for 10 seats of Ahmednagar District Central Cooperative Bank was conducted on Monday across 33 polling centres in Ahilyanagar district amid high political intensity as prominent regional leaders fight for control over the vital agrarian financial institution.Out of 21 seats of directors on the board, 11 were secured uncontested prior to the polls. The ruling cooperative panel, led by district guardian minister Radhakrishna Vikhe and former minister Balasaheb Thorat, secured 10 of these uncontested seats. The faction headed by Legislative Council Speaker Ram Shinde bagged one seat. This early edge gave the Vikhe-Thorat alliance a decisive majority even before the polling for the remaining segments.“A total of 27 candidates are in the fray for the 10 contested slots. A total of 3,809 voters out of 3,837 cast their votes on Monday. Results will be declared on Tuesday,” said returning officer Mangesh Suravse, also the district deputy registrar of Ahilyanagar.High-profile electoral battles were seen in constituencies such as Akole, Karjat and Parner, where supporters of Lok Sabha MP Nilesh Lanke and former MP Sadashiv Lokhande fielded candidates against the Vikhe-Thorat panel.In Karjat, the Vikhe-Thorat panel is pitted against the Ram Shinde-led panel in a direct contest.After casting his vote, NCP (SP) MP Lanke said, “It is a battle between the established and the deprived, and we have the habit of taking on the established ones and defeating them.” He said contesting was vital to ensure the survival of the bank.Former MP Sujay Vikhe said voters support cooperation over party-level politics, prompting leaders Radhakrishna Vikhe, Balasaheb Thorat and NCP MLA Sangram Jagtap to form a consensus panel. “The voters have always refused party-level politics and instead supported people on the basis of their work. Since people here support cooperation, you can see we joined hands to have a panel to evolve a consensus, and we believe we have been successful,” said Sujay Vikhe.Returning officer Suravse ordered that a police complaint be lodged over a breach of voting secrecy at centre number 27 in Bhikaji Tukaram Meher Secondary School in Sangamner, as a video circulated on social media showing a voter revealing his ballot paper inside the booth. Another person allegedly recorded his act on a cellphone.Suravse directed regional officer Santosh Kore and centre head Dilip Chature to submit an incident report and file an FIR against both individuals at the local police station for violating the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Election Rules 2014 and sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: Out of 21 seats of directors on the board, 11 were secured uncontested prior to the polls. The ruling cooperative panel, led by district guardian minister Radhakrishna Vikhe and former minister Balasaheb Thorat, secured 10 of these uncontested seats. The faction headed by Legislative Council Speaker Ram Shinde bagged one seat.

Article Title: Robbers loot Rs 3 crore from courier vehicle on Mumbai-Agra highway in Dhule
Article Text:
Nashik:





A gang of five to six robbers intercepted a courier SUV on Mumbai-Agra highway near Palasner village in Dhule and fled with Rs 3.06 crore between 12.30am and 12.45am on Saturday. SUV driver told police that the robbers smashed the window with iron rods, dragged him out, assaulted and blindfolded him before forcing him and his colleague into their vehicle.The Shirpur Taluka police have registered an FIR under relevant sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for robbery, assault and wrongful confinement. Inspector Jaypal Hire said, “Three teams have been formed to ascertain the identity of the criminals involved in the robbery and trace them.”“Owing to the Diwali holidays, employees at the firm’s Bhopal branch had been directed to transfer cash collections to its Mumbai office,” police said.Acting on the instructions, two employees left Bhopal around 6pm on Friday in an SUV carrying the cash. After entering Maharashtra around 12.15am, their SUV was intercepted by a multipurpose vehicle (MPV) near Palasner.In his complaint, the SUV driver said five to six men got out of the MPV, smashed the driver’s-side window using iron pipes and rods, dragged him out and assaulted him.The attackers allegedly blindfolded him and forced him into their vehicle before driving away.The complainant told police that the MPV halted briefly at a location before moving again. “Later, both he and his colleague, who had also been blindfolded, were pushed out of the vehicle. The assailants handed over the keys to their SUV, but the vehicle was not nearby,” police said, citing the complaint.The duo walked to a nearby village, contacted firm officials using a villager’s cellphone and began searching for the SUV. “They eventually located the vehicle, but a bag containing Rs 3.06 crore was missing,” police said.Police said investigations were under way and suspected the accused might have fled back to neighbouring Madhya Pradesh. “Three teams have been formed to ascertain the identity of the criminals involved in the robbery and trace them,” inspector Hire said.
Article Summary: A gang of five to six robbers intercepted a courier SUV on Mumbai-Agra highway near Palasner village in Dhule. SUV driver told police that the robbers smashed the window with iron rods, dragged him out, assaulted and blindfolded him before forcing him and his colleague into their vehicle.

Article Title: Man robbed of Rs 40,000 in autorickshaw
Article Text:
Nashik

:





A 49-year-old man from Khambgaon in Buldhana district was robbed of Rs 40,000 by three unidentified men while travelling in an autorickshaw in Nashik city on Friday morning.Based on his complaint, the Panchavati police registered a robbery case against three unidentified suspects.The incident took place between 7am and 7.30am in the Panchavati Karanja area. The victim had come to Nashik by bus for some work and hired an autorickshaw in which three men were already seated.As the autorickshaw proceeded, the driver took a different route. The three men then allegedly pulled out a knife and threatened the victim with dire consequences if he did not hand over his money.The victim handed over Rs 20,000 in cash. The suspects also forced him to transfer another Rs 20,000 online before pushing him out of the autorickshaw and fleeing, police said.
Article Summary: A 49-year-old man from Khambgaon in Buldhana district was robbed of Rs 40,000 by three unidentified men. The incident took place between 7am and 7.30am in the Panchavati Karanja area.

Article Title: Former AIADMK MLA, others booked for insulting and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri
Article Text: DHARMAPURI: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against A Govindasamy, former Pappireddipatti AIADMK MLA, and others on charges of humiliating and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri.The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months. In his complaint, Arunkumar stated that Govindasamy and his accomplices, numbering more than 30, arrived at the petrol bunk around 10.45am on Oct 26.Arunkumar alleged that the former MLA obstructed vehicles entering the bunk for refuelling and verbally abused him using obscene language and caste-based slurs. Arunkumar stated that his coworker, Nandakumar, who questioned the behaviour, was also assaulted by those who accompanied the former MLA.Arunkumar approached the Dharmapuri superintendent of police A K Arun Kabilan on Friday seeking action against Govindasamy and others under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Following an inquiry led by Dharmapuri deputy superintendent of Police Sivaraman, a case was registered against the former MLA and others at the Dharmapuri Town B-1 police station.
Article Summary: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: 82-year-old woman injured as robbers snatch 11 sovereigns of gold
Article Text:
82-year-old woman injured as robbers snatch 11 sovereigns of gold

Madurai

:





An 82-year-old woman sustained severe injuries after unidentified intruders broke into her house in M Paraiyangulam village near Thiruchuli in Virudhunagar district at midnight and snatched 11 sovereigns of gold jewellery from her.The victim, identified as Muthukaruppayi, was asleep when the intruders broke into her house. They forcibly snatched a four-sovereign gold chain from her neck and ripped off a seven-sovereign gold ear ornament, tearing her ears in the process, before fleeing.Hearing her cries for help, neighbours rushed to the house and found her bleeding from her ears. They rescued her and took her to Aruppukottai Government Hospital, where she is undergoing treatment.A Mukkulam police, along with Thiruchuli deputy superintendent of police Pradeep , visited the crime scene. Police registered a case and formed a special team to examine CCTV footage in the area and identify the robbers.
Article Summary: The victim, identified as Muthukaruppayi, was asleep when the intruders broke into her house. They forcibly snatched a four-sovereign gold chain from her neck. Neighbours rushed to the house and found her bleeding from her ears. She is undergoing treatment at Aruppukottai Government Hospital.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: Materials including watch worth Rs 1.9 lakh goes missing from court strongroom
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Case materials including a watch worth nearly Rs 1.9 lakh have gone missing from a storage facility of the Ernakulam district court complex. As per the FIR, items linked to 124 cases have gone missing.Ernakulam Central Police registered an FIR on Oct 29 under section relating to theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master. The accused is yet to be traced.Police sources said the theft came to light after the court approved a claim petition filed last month by a woman industrialist from Kochi seeking the release of her husband’s watch. The watch was part of a 2016 case in which a gang allegedly threatened the industrialist and took away a luxury car and the watch, together worth Rs 1.5 crore. South Police had recovered the items from a moneylender in Thrissur’s Triprayar.The watch was found missing when court officials checked the storage facility to release it. A subsequent examination of records, including audit reports, revealed that materials in 123 other cases were also missing.A case was registered based on a complaint by the junior superintendent of JFCM-II Court. The documents and articles related to cases are suspected to have gone missing between Jan 1, 2016, and Sept 21, 2026.The room where the case properties were stored had reportedly been shifted at some point. Investigators will examine court registers to determine whether the items went missing. CCTV footage is also being scrutinised and statements will be recorded from court staff, including the employee responsible for the strongroom.
Article Summary: Case materials including a watch worth nearly Rs 1.9 lakh have gone missing from a storage facility of the Ernakulam district court complex. The watch was part of a 2016 case in which a gang allegedly threatened the industrialist and took away a luxury car and the watch. The accused is yet to be traced.

Article Title: KSRTC told to pay Rs 45,000 compensation to passenger injured during vacation trip
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Ernakulam consumer grievance redressal forum has ordered Kerala State Road Transport Corporation ( KSRTC ) to pay Rs 45,000 compensation to a passenger injured during a vacation trip to Malakkapara in Oct 2023.The order followed a complaint filed by the wife of the injured 73-year-old Edapally resident. A residents’ association had organised the trip in a KSRTC bus.According to the complaint, the bus crew asked the elderly passenger to move to another seat, saying passengers boarding at Angamaly had booked the seat he initially occupied. As he was moving, the driver suddenly applied the brakes, causing him to fall on the bus floor and fracture a bone in his left wrist.He was taken to hospital and underwent surgery, with his family spending Rs 50,000 on treatment. The complainant alleged that KSRTC had failed to provide proper service. The forum issued its order after examining hospital documents.KSRTC has been operating vacation trips to tourist destinations under its budget tourism initiative since 2021. The cash-strapped corporation uses the initiative, which has been highly successful, to increase revenue. However, multiple incidents involving its buses have recently raised concerns.
Article Summary: KSRTC ordered to pay Rs 45,000 compensation to a passenger injured during a vacation trip to Malakkapara in Oct 2023. The order followed a complaint filed by the wife of the injured 73-year-old Edapally resident. A residents’ association had organised the trip in a KSRTC bus.
